newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat closes lower on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat closes lower on fund selling.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended broadly lower on successive waves of fund-selling that were sparked when CBOT soybeans failed to effectively break a resistance level, traders said.

"Soybeans failed to hold on to their higher levels (above $8.00 in the November contract)," a trader said. "With outside markets showing technically weak price action, the funds opted to clear out of the positions they took on last week."
KCBT wheat ended 4-3/4 to 11-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with Sept down seven cents at $4.75-1/2. Dec lost 10-1/2 cents to close at $4.73-1/2.
Traders said Wednesday's lower close made it likely that Thursday's market would test the six-month lows set last week.
Rosenthal Collins topped the list of sellers on the players' sheet, selling 3.5 million December bushels. Traders said RC was clearing out of the December position it assumed last week.
Refco and LFG each sold at least 1.2 million Dec, and Continental and FIMAT each sold one million Dec, traders said. FIMAT also bear-spread 1.2 million Dec/Sept.
KCBT estimated wheat volume at 44.965 million bushels Wednesday, versus 31.74 million Tuesday.
